item.title: In an Annual Property Trigger, Separate Living Change From Ownership Change
item.description: A moving Property Palace does not automatically mean a purchase or sale. Housing arrangements, repairs, and shared space often move before legal ownership does.

item.title: When Life and Body Both Look Strong, Let the Wealth Palace Decide Monetization
item.description: A strong Life Palace and Body Palace do not automatically reveal the best income path. Preference, effort, and monetization still need to be separated.

item.title: When the Annual Travel Palace Moves, Read Platform Before City
item.description: An activated Travel Palace often shifts platform, clients, or outside access before it turns into a literal move. Separate those layers before naming the city decision.

item.title: When the Opposite Axis Is Strong but Support Is Thin, Read for Landing First
item.description: A bright axis does not guarantee real-world delivery. When the opposite palace is strong and support is weak, check whether the main line can actually land.

item.title: In an Empty Palace, Keep the Subject Before You Borrow the Opposite Tone
item.description: An empty palace should keep its own subject first. The opposite palace can lend tone, but it should not replace the life area you are actually judging.

item.title: Yue Lang Tian Men Is Not Too Gentle. It Fails When Clarity Turns Murky
item.description: Yue Lang Tian Men is powerful through clarity and steadiness, not loudness. Its real risk is losing clear judgment, not appearing gentle on the surface.

item.title: Ban Kong Zhe Chi: What Kind of Slowdown Should You Guard First?
item.description: Ban Kong Zhe Chi is more useful when you separate re-routing failure, broken support, and lost inner momentum instead of repeating one vague warning about midlife.

item.title: Tuo Luo in the Travel Palace: Is the Delay in Paperwork, Route, or Decision?
item.description: Tuo Luo in the Travel Palace often means drag rather than disaster. Separate paperwork delay, route friction, and hesitant action before naming the real problem.

item.title: Opposite Palace or Four Directions First? Start With Axis or Support
item.description: Choose the reading order by the question itself: axis questions need the opposite palace early, while support questions often start with the wider receiving structure.

item.title: Why an Empty Palace Borrows Tone Before It Borrows Outcome
item.description: An empty palace can borrow the first tone from the opposite palace, but resources and outcomes still need the wider structure before you make a claim.

item.title: Life Palace Hua Quan: Start With Support Structure Before You Call It Pressure
item.description: Life Palace Hua Quan is not just a personality label. The real distinction is whether the decision line has support, handoff, and shared accountability after the first move.

item.title: When the Parent Palace Activates, Is It Paperwork or Elders First?
item.description: An activated Parent Palace often raises approvals, paperwork, and household rules before it clearly turns into an elder-care event. Separate the institutional line from the family line early.

item.title: A Good Annual Cycle With No Result Yet? Check Which Palace Was Actually Lit Up
item.description: An annual cycle can be favorable without rewarding the exact life area you were watching. Start by checking whether the activated palace matches the question you care about.

item.title: Read Responsibility Before Industry in the Career Palace
item.description: The Career Palace works better as a responsibility map than a job-title catalog. Industry and title usually come after role, authority, and work structure are separated.

item.title: In a Crowded Palace, Read the Main Star Before the Transformations
item.description: A crowded palace becomes clearer when the main star names the operating pattern first, the Four Transformations mark emphasis second, and support or friction comes later.
